Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement. Asset Purchase Agreement On November 23, 2026, JP Enterprises Holdings, LLC, a Utah limited liability company and a wholly owned indirect subsidiary of Alta Equipment Group Inc., a Delaware corporation (“Alta” or the “Company”), and certain other indirect subsidiaries of Alta (collectively, the “Buyers”), Jackson Group Peterbilt, Inc., a Utah corporation (“JGP”), the other sellers party thereto (together with JGP, the “Sellers”), the BKJ 2016 Irrevocable Trust (the “Seller Trust”) and Blake Jackson (the “Principal” and, together with the Sellers and the Seller Trust, the “Seller Parties”) agreed that, pursuant to an Asset Purchase Agreement (the “Asset Purchase Agreement”), the Buyers would acquire, and the Sellers would sell, substantially all of the assets used or held for use in the Sellers’ commercial truck and trailer dealership business and assume certain specified liabilities, on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth therein (the “Acquisition” or the “Transaction”). The Sellers operate a network of Peterbilt and other original equipment manufacturer (“OEM”) dealerships in Colorado, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, Oregon, Utah, Washington and Wyoming, providing sales, leasing, rental, servicing, customization, parts distribution, maintenance and financing services. The aggregate purchase price for the purchased assets (the “Purchase Price”) is $272.5 million plus a net tangible asset adjustment, subject to a post-closing true-up. At the closing of the Acquisition (the “Closing”), $30,000,000 of the Purchase Price will be paid through the issuance of approximately 4,739,336 shares of Alta common stock, par value $0.0001 per share (“Alta common stock”), valued at a fixed price of $6.33 per share (the “Share Consideration”), and the balance will be paid in cash (the “Cash Consideration”). The Share Consideration will be issued to the Seller Trust and certain other affiliates of the Principal, as directed by the Sellers. The Buyers previously paid a $1.0 million deposit will be credited against the Purchase Price at Closing. At Closing, $5.0 million of the Cash Consideration will be deposited into escrow to secure specified purchase price adjustment and indemnification obligations of the Sellers. In connection with the Acquisition, the Buyers or their designee will also purchase specified real property in Cheyenne, Wyoming from an affiliate of the Sellers for $3.4 million, plus reimbursement of specified construction costs incurred through closing, in addition to the purchase price payable under the Asset Purchase Agreement. The transaction arrangements also contemplate sales of certain other dealership properties by affiliates of the Sellers to third-party purchasers and the Buyers’ entry into new leases for those properties. Consummation of the Acquisition is subject to the satisfaction or waiver of specified conditions, including, among others: (i) receipt of required Company stockholder approval of the related securities issuances; (ii) receipt of financing and required lender consents satisfactory to the Buyers; (iii) receipt of required OEM and PacLease approvals and dealership and floor plan financing arrangements; (iv) receipt of applicable state dealer licensing approvals; (v) the Sellers’ business having Adjusted TTM Pre-Tax Net Income, as defined in the Asset Purchase Agreement, of at least $41.0 million; (vi) satisfaction of specified conditions relating to the related real property transactions; and (vii) other customary conditions, including the accuracy of representations and warranties, performance of covenants and absence of a material adverse effect on the Sellers’ business, in each case subject to the standards set forth in the Asset Purchase Agreement. The Asset Purchase Agreement contains customary representations, warranties and covenants, including covenants relating to the conduct of the Sellers’ business in the ordinary course before the Closing, access to information, restrictions on solicitation of alternative acquisition proposals, employee matters, obtaining governmental and OEM approvals and cooperation with financing and public company disclosures. The Seller Parties and the Buyers have agreed to indemnify one another for specified losses, subject to negotiated limitations, including a $1,000,000 deductible and, for the Seller Parties’ non-fundamental representation and warranty breaches, a cap of 10% of the Purchase Price, in each case subject to specified exceptions. At the Closing, the Seller Parties will enter into restrictive covenant agreements providing for five-year non-competition and non-solicitation restrictions, subject to specified exceptions. The Buyers are required, at their expense, to file a registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”) registering the resale of the Share Consideration within 120 days after the Closing. The Asset Purchase Agreement provides for termination rights, including termination by mutual written consent, for certain uncured breaches, if specified closing conditions have not been or will not be satisfied by January 6, 2027 (the “Outside Date”), or if a final legal prohibition prevents the Acquisition. The Buyers may extend the Outside Date for specified delays in Peterbilt Motors Company’s dealer and floor plan financing approvals after November 20, 2026 and for delays in the Alta stockholder vote resulting from SEC review of the preliminary proxy statement, with such extensions being cumulative. Peterbilt Motors Company also has a contractual right of first refusal under its dealer agreements, the exercise of which permits termination without a termination fee or other damages. On November 21, 2026, Peterbilt Motors Company provided Conditional Approval (as described under Item 8.01 below) with respect to the Acquisition and waived its right of first refusal under the Sellers’ dealer agreements. Upon termination of the Asset Purchase Agreement, the Buyers may in certain circumstances, including if Alta stockholders do not approve the securities issuances or the Buyers fail to obtain financing, be required to pay the Sellers a termination fee of $9,000,000 (the “Termination Fee”), subject to exceptions for specified OEM approval failures, Seller failures to close or material breaches, and failures of mutual or Buyers’ closing conditions other than the financing and lender approval, Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended (the “HSR Act”) waiting period and Buyers’ board or stockholder approval conditions, subject to the terms of the agreement. Subject to the exceptions and limitations set forth in the Asset Purchase Agreement, the Termination Fee is the Seller Parties’ sole and exclusive remedy against the Buyers and their affiliates following termination, and their aggregate liability following termination is limited as provided in the Asset Purchase Agreement. On November 2, 2026, Alta and the PIPE Investors (as defined below) entered into a side letter agreement pursuant to which the PIPE Investors agreed to backstop all or a portion of this termination fee in certain circumstances and subject to certain conditions. The $1,000,000 deposit is non-refundable except in specified circumstances involving Seller fraud. The foregoing description of the Asset Purchase Agreement does not purport to be complete and is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the Asset Purchase Agreement, which is filed as Exhibit 2.1 to this Current Report on Form 8-K and is incorporated herein by reference. Stock Purchase Agreement In connection with the Acquisition, on November 23, 2026, Alta entered into a Stock Purchase Agreement (the “Stock Purchase Agreement”) with DRAGSA 120 LLC and DRAGSA 120-IV LLC, investors affiliated with Viking Global Investors LP (collectively, the “PIPE Investors”). Pursuant to the Stock Purchase Agreement, Alta agreed to issue and sell to the PIPE Investors an aggregate of 534,597 shares of non-voting Series B Convertible Preferred Stock, par value $0.0001 per share (the “PIPE Preferred Stock”), for aggregate gross proceeds of approximately $338.4 million, at a purchase price of $633 per share (the “PIPE Financing” and, together with the Acquisition, the “Transactions”). Each share of PIPE Preferred Stock will initially be convertible into 100 shares of Alta common stock (the shares issuable upon conversion, the “PIPE Shares”), subject to the terms and limitations described below. Alta intends to use the proceeds to fund a portion of the Cash Consideration, including the related acquisition of the Cheyenne, Wyoming real property, fund amounts payable in connection with a related real estate lease, pay expenses related to the PIPE Financing and for working capital and general corporate purposes. The closing of the PIPE Financing (the “PIPE Closing”) is expected to occur substantially concurrently with the Closing and is conditioned upon prior or substantially simultaneous consummation of the Acquisition. The PIPE Closing is subject to additional conditions, including, among others, Alta stockholder approval for the issuance of the PIPE Preferred Stock and the PIPE Shares (the “Share Issuance Proposal”), expiration or termination of applicable HSR Act waiting periods, the accuracy of representations and warranties subject to certain qualifications and performance of covenants in all material respects. The PIPE Investors’ obligations are further conditioned upon, among other things, the absence of a continuing Company Material Adverse Effect (as defined in the Stock Purchase Agreement), filing and acceptance of the Certificate of Designations described below, reservation and NYSE listing approval of the PIPE Shares, subject to official notice of issuance, and a condition relating to specified terminations or outstanding termination notices under material OEM contracts. Alta has agreed to seek stockholder approval of the Share Issuance Proposal pursuant to Section 312.03 of the NYSE Listed Company Manual. The Company’s board of directors (the “Board”) has unanimously approved the Transactions and recommends that stockholders approve the Share Issuance Proposal, subject to the provisions of the Stock Purchase Agreement permitting a change in recommendation in specified circumstances. The Company and the PIPE Investors will enter into a registration rights agreement at the PIPE Closing providing registration rights with respect to the securities covered thereby. The Stock Purchase Agreement contains customary representations, warranties and covenants. The PIPE Investors are subject to a six-month restriction on transfers of PIPE Preferred Stock and the underlying Alta common stock without the consent of the Board, excluding the directors appointed by the PIPE Investors (as discussed below), subject to customary exceptions. Following the six-month period, transfers of PIPE Preferred Stock remain subject to advance consultation with the Board and prior written Board approval for transfers to competitors, subject to specified exceptions (including that these consultation and approval requirements do not apply to transfers of Alta common stock, including PIPE Shares issued upon conversion of PIPE Preferred Stock). The PIPE Investors have also agreed to standstill restrictions, subject to specified exceptions, until the later of the first anniversary of the PIPE Closing and the time when the PIPE Investors and their permitted transferees collectively beneficially own less than 15% of Alta’s outstanding common stock, calculated on an as-converted basis and without giving effect to any limitations on conversion of the PIPE Preferred Stock. For so long as the PIPE Investors and their permitted transferees collectively continue to beneficially own at least 10% of the PIPE Preferred Stock purchased at the PIPE Closing, including PIPE Shares issued upon conversion, calculated on an as-converted basis, they will have the right to appoint one non-voting Board observer, subject to specified exclusions from meetings and information access. The Stock Purchase Agreement provides termination rights for Alta and the PIPE Investors, including, among others, termination by mutual agreement, for a final legal prohibition, if the PIPE Closing has not occurred by June 30, 2027, if requisite stockholder approval is not obtained, for certain uncured breaches, or following termination of the Asset Purchase Agreement. The PIPE Investors may also terminate following specified changes in the recommendation of the Board or Alta’s or a subsidiary’s entry into an agreement providing for an alternative acquisition transaction. Alta may terminate the Stock Purchase Agreement in order to enter into a definitive agreement providing for a Superior Proposal (as defined in the Stock Purchase Agreement), subject to specified conditions, including payment of the applicable termination fee. Under the Stock Purchase Agreement, Alta has agreed to reimburse the PIPE Investors for reasonable, documented out-of-pocket legal fees and expenses, up to $3,384,000, at the PIPE Closing or upon termination of the Stock Purchase Agreement in specified circumstances. The Stock Purchase Agreement also provides that Alta may be required to pay the PIPE Investors a termination fee of $9,000,000, less the expense reimbursement amount, upon termination in specified circumstances, including those relating to a change in the recommendation of the Board, Alta’s or a subsidiary’s entry into an alternative acquisition agreement or certain subsequent acquisition transactions. Subject to the exceptions and limitations set forth in the Stock Purchase Agreement, the termination fee, together with the applicable expense reimbursement, is the PIPE Investors’ sole and exclusive remedy against Alta and the other related parties specified in the Stock Purchase Agreement for losses arising from the failure to consummate the transactions contemplated thereby. These obligations are separate from the termination fee payable to the Sellers under the Asset Purchase Agreement. The foregoing description of the Stock Purchase Agreement does not purport to be complete and is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the Stock Purchase Agreement, which is filed as Exhibit 10.1 to this Current Report on Form 8-K and is incorporated herein by reference. Certificate of Designations At the PIPE Closing, Alta will file with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware a Certificate of Designations establishing the rights, preferences and limitations of the PIPE Preferred Stock (the “Certificate of Designations”). The PIPE Preferred Stock will have no maturity date, no voting rights, except as required by law or expressly provided in the Certificate of Designations, no fixed or cumulative dividend and no liquidation preference, and will not be redeemable at the option of Alta or any holder. The PIPE Preferred Stock will participate in dividends and other distributions on Alta common stock and distributions upon liquidation, dissolution or winding up on an as-converted basis, without regard to conversion limitations, subject to the terms of the Certificate of Designations. It will rank on parity with Alta common stock on that basis and junior to Alta’s 10% Series A Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock and other securities expressly designated as senior, as well as Alta’s indebtedness and the indebtedness and other liabilities of its existing subsidiaries. Each holder may convert its PIPE Preferred Stock, in whole or in part, at any time at an initial exchange ratio of 100 shares of Alta common stock for each share of PIPE Preferred Stock, subject to proportionate adjustments for stock splits, combinations and common stock dividends and provisions governing specified reorganizations. All outstanding PIPE Preferred Stock will automatically convert upon election of the holders of a majority of the then-outstanding PIPE Preferred Stock. Both optional and automatic conversions are subject to required antitrust approvals and a limitation prohibiting conversion to the extent that the holder, together with any other persons whose beneficial ownership of Alta common stock would be aggregated with that holder for purposes of Section 13(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, and applicable SEC regulations, including any group of which that holder is a member (such persons, the holder’s “Attribution Parties”), would beneficially own more than 49.9% of the outstanding Alta common stock immediately after conversion (the “Beneficial Ownership Limitation”). Shares not converted because of that limitation remain outstanding, retain their rights and remain convertible to the extent subsequently permitted. Upon specified changes of control in which common stockholders receive consideration, holders will receive the same kind and amount of consideration on an as-converted basis, without actual conversion and without regard to the Beneficial Ownership Limitation or the Voting Cap described below. The PIPE Preferred Stock will be non-voting except as required by Delaware law or expressly provided in the Certificate of Designations. Holders will have one vote per share when voting as a separate series and will vote on an as-converted basis when required by Delaware law to vote together with the common stock or another class or series. The PIPE Investors, together with their Attribution Parties, may not cast votes with respect to Alta common stock exceeding 49.9% of its total voting power on any matter (the “Voting Cap”). While any PIPE Preferred Stock remains outstanding, the affirmative vote or written consent of holders of a majority of that series will be required for specified adverse amendments to Alta’s organizational documents or the rights of the PIPE Preferred Stock, changes to the authorized number of shares of PIPE Preferred Stock or Alta common stock, actions prohibiting or materially restricting Alta from honoring the preferred rights, and specified voluntary deregistration or delisting actions. Additional consent rights will apply while the PIPE Investors and their Attribution Parties hold at least 15% of the PIPE Preferred Stock purchased at the PIPE Closing or PIPE Shares issued upon conversion. Subject to the exceptions and thresholds set forth in the Certificate of Designations, these rights cover (i) authorizing or issuing equity or equity-linked securities; (ii) declaring or paying dividends or distributions, or redeeming or repurchasing capital stock; (iii) making specified changes to equity incentive plans or entering into or modifying specified related-party arrangements; (iv) changing the size of the Board or director voting rights; (v) commencing voluntary bankruptcy proceedings or liquidating, dissolving or winding up; (vi) making specified investments in new material lines of business or non-wholly owned subsidiaries; (vii) incurring, assuming or guaranteeing specified indebtedness; (viii) effecting mergers, consolidations, recapitalizations, acquisitions or asset dispositions; or (ix) hiring or terminating Alta’s chief executive officer or chief financial officer. For so long as the PIPE Investors, together with their Attribution Parties, hold at least 25% of the PIPE Preferred Stock purchased at the PIPE Closing or PIPE Shares issued upon conversion, they will collectively have the right to appoint two directors to the Board and the sole right to remove and replace those directors. The Board will be increased by two members at the PIPE Closing, and the initial appointees will take office at that time. These directors will not be subject to Alta’s classified board provisions and will have committee participation rights subject to specified independence, financial literacy and conflict-of-interest limitations. These appointment rights are not subject to the Beneficial Ownership Limitation or the Voting Cap. The Certificate of Designations also provides information rights while the 15% ownership threshold is met and pro rata participation rights in future equity issuances, subject to specified exceptions, with any participation exceeding the Beneficial Ownership Limitation to be issued as additional PIPE Preferred Stock rather than Alta common stock. The foregoing description of the Certificate of Designations does not purport to be complete and is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the form of Certificate of Designations, which is filed as Exhibit 3.1 to this Current Report on Form 8-K and is incorporated herein by reference. Voting Agreement In connection with the PIPE Financing, on November 23, 2026, Alta entered into a Voting Agreement (the “Voting Agreement”) with certain stockholders who owned, as of November 16, 2026, approximately 33% of the outstanding Alta common stock (the “Supporting Stockholders”). Subject to the Voting Agreement’s terms, the Supporting Stockholders agreed to vote their shares, including any additional voting securities acquired during its term, in favor of the stockholder approval required under NYSE listing standards for issuance of the PIPE Preferred Stock and the PIPE Shares, and any necessary adjournment to obtain a quorum or sufficient affirmative votes, and against specified actions that would cause a failure of closing conditions or a breach of Alta’s obligations under the Stock Purchase Agreement or prevent or materially delay the PIPE Financing. The Voting Agreement restricts transfers of the shares subject to the Voting Agreement without Alta’s prior written consent, subject to specified exceptions, including affiliate, limited partner, family and trust transfers for which the transferee agrees to be bound by the terms of the Voting Agreement, and specified legally required transfers. Hedging transactions are permitted if the Supporting Stockholder retains sole voting power and remains bound by its obligations. The agreement applies solely to the Supporting Stockholders in their capacities as stockholders and does not restrict their actions or fiduciary responsibilities as directors or officers. The Voting Agreement terminates upon the earliest of receipt of the required stockholder approval, termination of the Stock Purchase Agreement in accordance with its terms and a specified change in the recommendation of the Board, as provided in the Stock Purchase Agreement. The foregoing description of the Voting Agreement does not purport to be complete and is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the Voting Agreement, which is filed as Exhibit 10.2 to this Current Report on Form 8-K and is incorporated herein by reference. The agreements and the foregoing descriptions have been included to provide investors with information regarding their terms and are not intended to provide other factual information about Alta, the Sellers, the PIPE Investors or their respective subsidiaries or affiliates. The representations, warranties and covenants contained in the agreements were made solely for purposes of the applicable agreement, as of specified dates and for the benefit of its parties, and may be qualified by confidential disclosures and negotiated limitations and standards of materiality that differ from those applicable to investors. Investors should not rely on the representations, warranties and covenants, or any descriptions thereof, as characterizations of the actual state of facts or condition of any party. Information concerning their subject matter may change after the date of the applicable agreement, and subsequent information may or may not be fully reflected in Alta’s public disclosures. Item 3.02. Unregistered Sales of Equity Securities. The disclosure set forth in Item 1.01 of this Current Report on Form 8-K is incorporated by reference herein. The shares of Alta common stock to be issued as consideration in the Acquisition, the shares of PIPE Preferred Stock to be issued and sold in the PIPE Financing and the PIPE Shares have not been registered under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”), and will be issued in reliance upon the exemption from registration provided by Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act and/or Rule 506 of Regulation D promulgated thereunder. Item 5.02. Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers. Ryan Greenawalt The Company has entered into a new employment agreement with Ryan Greenawalt, its chief executive officer, dated November 20, 2026. Such employment agreement provides for (i) a base salary of $875,000, subject to review and adjustment by the Compensation Committee of the Board (the “Committee”), (ii) eligibility to earn an annual cash bonus with an initial target amount of 150% of base salary (with such target subject to review and adjustment by the Board, the Committee or a delegate of either) based upon achievement of objective and subjective criteria, (iii) eligibility to be granted an annual long-term incentive award as determined by the Board or Committee based upon Mr. Greenawalt’s or the Company’s achievement of performance criteria during the applicable performance period. For 2026, Mr. Greenawalt’s long-term incentive award will be an equity award with a grant date value equal to 275% of his base salary. The employment agreement provides that if Mr. Greenawalt is terminated by the Company without Cause (as defined in the agreement) or resigns for Good Reason (as defined in the agreement), then he will be entitled to (i) continued payment of base salary for 24 months after termination of employment, (ii) if he elects COBRA continuation payments, payment of an amount, net of taxes equal to any COBRA premiums for 24 months following termination (or such earlier date he receives coverage under another company plan), (iii) immediate vesting of unvested and outstanding equity awards and (iv) a pro-rata annual cash bonus for the year in which the termination occurs at the target amount, plus an additional cash bonus equal to two times (2.0) the target bonus percentage of base salary at the time of termination. The employment agreement also provides that if within twelve (12) months following a “Change in Control” (as defined in the agreement), Mr. Greenawalt is terminated by the Company without Cause, resigns for Good Reason or upon termination on account of death or disability, then Mr. Greenawalt will be entitled to (i) a lump sum payment of 36 months of base salary, (ii) if he elects COBRA continuation payments, payment of an amount, net of taxes equal to any COBRA premiums for 36 months following termination (or such earlier date he receives coverage under another company plan), (iii) unvested and outstanding equity award shall immediately vest, (iv) Mr. Greenawalt will receive a pro-rata annual cash bonus for the year in which the termination occurs at the target amount, plus an additional cash bonus equal to three-times the target bonus percentage of base salary at the time of termination. Any severance or other payments upon a termination of employment are subject to Mr. Greenawalt executing and not revoking a release of claims in a form acceptable to the Company. The employment agreement contains certain restrictive covenants, including nondisclosure of confidential information and a one-year post-termination non-compete and non-solicitation provision. The employment agreement provides that if any payments to Mr. Greenawalt constitute “parachute payments” under section 280G of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the “IRS Code”), then such payments will be reduced if such reductions would mean that no portion of the payments would be subject to the excise tax under section 4999 of the IRS Code, provided that, if all or a portion of such payments would result in an amount, after taking all taxes into account including the excise tax under section 4999, that would result in a greater after-tax benefit to Mr. Greenawalt, then he will receive such payments and pay the excise tax. For 2026, Mr. Colucci’s long-term incentive award will be an equity award with a grant date value equal to 70% of his base salary. Any severance or other payments upon a termination of employment are subject to Mr. Colucci executing and not revoking a release of claims in a form acceptable to the Company.
